AGENTS.md.content:
# exporter - for agents

> **This document owns:** the commands as the manifests name them, the conventions an agent cannot infer from the code of exporter, and the gotchas. Forty lines at most; the README links here for the commands and the docs index owns everything else. *(draft, review me)* - the commands are read from the manifests; conventions and gotchas are open questions

## Commands

- install: `npm ci` [package.json]
- run: `npm run dev:start` [package.json: scripts.dev:start]
- build: `npm run build` [package.json: scripts.build]
- test: `npm run test` [package.json: scripts.test]

## Conventions

- open question: branch, commit and PR rules an agent would get wrong without being told

## Gotchas

- open question: the thing that costs an afternoon here

## Docs

- [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md) - the map; read it before the folder.

CHANGELOG.md.why: GitHub surfaces a root CHANGELOG.md; one line pointing at docs/history/CHANGELOG.md

CONTRIBUTING.md.why: GitHub surfaces a root CONTRIBUTING.md; one line pointing at docs/guides/CONTRIBUTING.md

docs/INDEX.md.content:
# exporter docs

> An intentionally defective fixture. See ../README.md for why.

Pick the one file you need here; do not read the folder. Every doc says what it owns under its title; a fact has one home and the other docs link to it. State is one of `skeleton`, `draft`, `unreviewed`, `reviewed YYYY-MM-DD`, `none YYYY-MM-DD` (a person confirmed the doc says nothing applies here, so there is nothing to read), `stale YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Getting started

- [Onboarding](getting-started/ONBOARDING.md): the reading order for a new person, the path per role, and the vocabulary this repository uses. - skeleton
- [Setup](getting-started/SETUP.md): the path from a clean machine to a first visible success - prerequisites, install, run, what success looks like, and what to do when it fails. - unreviewed

## Guides

- [Development](guides/DEVELOPMENT.md): the daily loop of changing code here - run, debug, lint, test. How a change gets in (branch, commit, PR, review) is CONTRIBUTING's. - skeleton
- [Deployment](guides/DEPLOYMENT.md): how this is deployed - every deployable unit, its environment, the steps, and how to roll back. - skeleton
- [Testing](guides/TESTING.md): how this repository is tested — the runners, where tests live, how to run them, and what CI checks. - skeleton
- [Contributing](guides/CONTRIBUTING.md): how a change gets into this repository - branch and commit rules, the pull request, review, and the licence contributions fall under. What CI runs is TESTING's. - skeleton
- [Operations](guides/OPERATIONS.md): how this is run in production - health checks, alerts, what to do when each one fires, and who is on call. What runs unattended is JOBS's. - unreviewed

## Reference

- [Architecture](reference/ARCHITECTURE.md): the map of the system - its context, the containers it runs as, the building blocks inside them, how a request moves at runtime, how it is deployed, and the qualities and risks that shaped it. Decisions live in their own records. - skeleton
- [Configuration](reference/CONFIGURATION.md): every environment variable and flag this repository reads - its name, which unit reads it, whether it is required, and where its example lives. Names only, never a value. - skeleton
- [API reference](reference/API.md): the endpoints — path, method, auth, request and response shape, errors. The API is the contract; nobody reimplements it. - skeleton
- [Integrations](reference/INTEGRATIONS.md): every third party this repository talks to - what it is for, which unit calls it, and what breaks when it is down. The environment names are CONFIGURATION's. - skeleton
- [Security](reference/SECURITY.md): how a caller proves who it is, what a role may do, how secrets are handled, which data is sensitive, and the gaps known today. - skeleton
- [Jobs](reference/JOBS.md): what runs when nobody clicks - the background jobs, the queues, the schedules, the data flows between them, and the retry design. - skeleton

## Explanation

- [Product](explanation/PRODUCT.md): what the product is, who it is for, the idea it hangs on, how success is measured, its principles, and what it has said no to. Where it is going is ROADMAP's. - skeleton

## History

- [Changelog](history/CHANGELOG.md): the user-visible changes by version, newest first. Keep a Changelog headings; never drafted from commits. - unreviewed

## Root files

- [DEPLOY.md](../DEPLOY.md): The README links this file, so a reader reaches it in one hop - unreviewed

## Start here

Three files, in this order. Everything else is one hop from the second one.

1. **This file** - what exporter is and how the repository is laid out.
2. **[docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md)** - the index of every doc: what each one owns and its state. Pick the one file you need there; do not read the folder.
3. **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - the commands as the manifests name them, and the conventions a coding agent or a new contributor needs; forty lines at most.

What to read next is [docs/getting-started/ONBOARDING.md](docs/getting-started/ONBOARDING.md)'s once it is written (a skeleton today); until then, the first stops: [the commands](AGENTS.md#commands). The index says which file is which; this README keeps no list of its own, so the two cannot drift.

readme_append.content:
## What it is

*Three sentences at most: what it does, for whom, and the one idea it hangs on. The long form is PRODUCT's; link it.*
readme_append.heading: What it is

readme_append.content:
## Quickstart

*Numbered: a link to SETUP § Prerequisites, then install, run, the URL or command that proves it works. For an application the install and run commands are a checked copy of AGENTS.md § Commands; for a library or CLI they are the consumer's install and first call, a checked copy of PUBLIC_API § Install and import or CLI § Install and invoke - the one place a command is repeated, so a reader can start without a hop (R11 diffs the copy against its owner). SETUP owns the full path; this is the sixty-second version.*
readme_append.heading: Quickstart

readme_append.content:
## Repository layout

*A table, one row per top-level folder or unit: folder, what lives there, its own README when it has one. From the tree, never invented.*
readme_append.heading: Repository layout

readme_append.content:
## Commands

*One line and a link to AGENTS.md § Commands, which owns every command with its source. Never a second table here: a command with two homes drifts.*
readme_append.heading: Commands

readme_append.content:
## Status

*The file and field that hold the version (never the value, which changes every release), the licence file by name, the CI workflow by name. One line each.*
readme_append.heading: Status
